question: A boat can travel at a speed of 30 km/h in still water. If the flow of the stream is 2 km/h. How long will it take by the boat to travel 56 km upstream?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream

Upstream Speed = 30 − 2 = 28 km/h

Time = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed = 56 ÷ 28 = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water = 30 km/h

Speed of stream = 2 km/h

Distance to travel upstream = 56 km

 
 

 Distance = 56 km
 

 
• 
 

 Boat = 30 km/h
 
• 
 

 Stream = 2 km/h
 
• 
 

 Upstream Speed = 30 - 2 = 28 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Upstream Speed = Boat Speed − Stream Speed

Time = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream speed = 30 − 2 = 28 km/h

⇒ Time taken = 56 ÷ 28

⇒ Time taken = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When the boat travels along the direction of the stream, Downstream Speed = Boat Speed + Stream Speed.

Boat Speed in Still Water

If Downstream Speed (D) and Upstream Speed (U) are given, Boat Speed = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Stream Speed

If Downstream Speed (D) and Upstream Speed (U) are given, Stream Speed = (D − U) ÷ 2.
